exercises.title: Breadth first, depth first
exercises.task: Read BFS (a queue: visits nodes by distance, remembers each node's parent) and DFS (recursion: goes as deep as it can, then backs up). Run prints both visiting orders on a small map of towns, and the fewest-hops path BFS finds.

exercises.title: Shortest path in hops
exercises.task: Fill ShortestPath: a BFS from from that records each node's parent, then walks the parents back from to. Return nil if to cannot be reached.
hints: Mark a node as seen when you enqueue it, not when you dequeue it: otherwise it can be queued several times.
parent[next] = cur when you first see next. The start has no parent.
To build the path, start at to, follow parent until from, then reverse the slice.

exercises.title: Find a circular definition
exercises.task: A dictionary defines each word with other words. A circular definition (big means large, large means great, great means big) explains nothing. Return one cycle as a path that starts and ends on the same word, like [a b c a], or nil if there is none. DFS finds it: a cycle is an edge back to a node still on the current path.
hints: Three states per node: not visited, on the current path (in progress), done. An edge to an in-progress node closes a cycle.
Keep the current path in a slice (push on entry, pop on exit): when you find the edge back to node x, the cycle is the part of the path from x, plus x again.
Start a DFS from every node not yet done (in sorted order, for a predictable answer): the graph may have several parts.
